name: Numbers and Strings
description: For each integer $$$x$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, we will form the string $$$S(x)$$$ according to the following rules: compute $$$(x+1)$$$; write $$$x$$$ and $$$x+1$$$ next to each other in the decimal system without separators and leading zeros; in the resulting string, sort all digits in non-decreasing order. For example, the string $$$S(139)$$$ is 011349 (before sorting the digits, it is 139140 ). The string $$$S(99)$$$ is 00199 . Your task is to count the number of distinct strings among $$$S(1), S(2), \dots, S(n)$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of one line containing a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^{9} - 2$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the number of distinct strings among $$$S(1), S(2), \dots, S(n)$$$.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2104F — Numbers and Strings [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
